entries.definition: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and faintly grudging, it certifies that a thing can be put into practice without claiming it will go well, unlike *viable*.

entries.definition: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest endorsement here - it declares a plan sound enough to go ahead on as things stand, where *workable* says only that it will function.

entries.definition: capable of being done with means at hand and circumstances as they are
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Modest and practical - it promises the thing will function, not that it will succeed.

entries.definition: serenely self-possessed and free from agitation especially in times of stress
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving of steadiness held on purpose - the serenity is a bearing kept up while the pressure is on, not the luck of an easy hour.
examples: the performer seemed completely composed as she stepped onto the stage
I felt calm and more composed than I had in a long time

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word of the family - mildly approving, naming the absence of agitation without the lift *serene* gives the same state.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flatly descriptive: it registers that agitation is absent without crediting anyone for holding it off.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Raises the same unagitated state into something luminous and admired, where *calm* merely reports it.
examples: he remained serene in the midst of turbulence
a serene expression on her face

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The stillest word here - the self-possession sounds effortless rather than exerted, unlike the braced steadiness of *composed*.

entries.definition: not easily perturbed or excited or upset; marked by extreme calm and composure
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Stately and strong: it describes calm that cannot be shaken, not merely calm that happens to be unshaken.
examples: hitherto imperturbable, he now showed signs of alarm

entries.definition: not easily perturbed or excited or upset; marked by extreme calm and composure
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and warmly admiring where *imperturbable* is dignified, praising the same immunity to upset in cheerful terms.

entries.definition: in full control of your faculties
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain approval for having one's faculties gathered and in hand - steady rather than impressive.
examples: the witness remained collected throughout the cross-examination

entries.definition: in full control of your faculties
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal, and it prizes evenness above all: control that holds the level rather than control that shows.

entries.definition: in full control of your faculties
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Adds bearing to the control - the faculties are not just held but held gracefully, which *collected* never claims.
examples: perfectly poised and sure of himself

entries.definition: in full control of your faculties
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Credits the control explicitly to the person exercising it, sounding more effortful than the smooth *poised*.

entries.definition: in full control of your faculties
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises control that needs nothing from anyone else, with a reserve at its edge that *poised* does not carry.
examples: more self-contained and more dependable than many of the early frontiersmen

entries.definition: in full control of your faculties
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Weightier than *collected*: the faculties are owned rather than merely gathered, and the ownership is the compliment.
examples: strong and self-possessed in the face of trouble

entries.definition: marked by calm self-control (especially in trying circumstances); unemotional
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal approval with a chill in it - the self-control reads as unbothered, and the unemotional side can tip into indifference.

entries.definition: marked by calm self-control (especially in trying circumstances); unemotional
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the weight on judgement rather than temperature, praising the head that keeps working when circumstances turn trying.
